paper.title: GASP: Guided Asymmetric Self-Play For Coding LLMs
paper.central_claim: Guided Asymmetric Self-Play: teacher generates an easier lemma then harder lift variant of hard real-data goalpost questions so self-play is grounded; improves pass@20 on LiveCodeBench over unguided asymmetric self-play.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref=null: claude-kimi worker run, no per-call receipt exposed to the worker; model type per template (haiku slot -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]).

rationale: 师生共享同一权重、仅更新权重；引导题为RL训练数据而非非权重组件，按A3判范围外，不打分。

evidence.quote: differ only by role prompting; all updates are applied to the same weights.
evidence.support_explanation: Teacher and student are the same weights; every update is a weight update.

evidence.quote: For RL updates, we use Task-Relative REINFORCE++ as proposed in Absolute Zero
evidence.support_explanation: Training is RL on weights; lemma/lift questions are RL training data.

evidence.quote: questions should be challenging yet solvable for the student.
evidence.support_explanation: Teacher reward is learnability of generated questions; the retained product is the trained model.

evidence.quote: our framework uses a fixed set of goalposts.
evidence.support_explanation: The goalpost set is a fixed evaluation-derived training subset, not a retained, edited harness artifact.

signatures.object: Single Qwen2.5-Coder-7B weight set in teacher and student roles; 146 fixed goalpost questions as guidance
signatures.information: Hard LiveCodeBench pre-2024.08 goalposts (pass@100=0 after RL/AZR filtering); student pass-rate bands
signatures.operation: Teacher writes easier lemma then harder lift question from goalpost; rejection by pass band and cosine novelty
signatures.persistence: Weights; buffers only for novelty checks
signatures.claimed_effect: +2.5 pass@20 over AZR; 11 of 146 goalposts solved
signatures.failure_boundary: No validation that stepping stones align with goalpost; fixed goalpost set

gap.author_gap: Asymmetric self-play is goal-agnostic: hard problems are not necessarily informative for downstream capability.
